reason: Upstream uses the Temporal polyfill only to turn a wall time in a named zone into an instant (earlier instant in an overlap, no instant in a gap), to read local calendar fields and to step dates; Go's time package does all of that except the gap and overlap choice, which a small harness resolver defines, with zone data embedded through time/tzdata.

Upstream asks the rrule library only to list candidate wall times of one period and does validation, limits, time-zone mapping and end conditions in 689 lines of its own code; the Go design writes that candidate listing itself as part of one bounded evaluator on the time package, so no recurrence module is needed.

It exists only because of JavaScript: the experimental package that runs the host in a browser Web Worker needs synchronous SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 for its stand-in of node:crypto, and the browser's own hashing interface is asynchronous. Go's hashes are synchronous and pure Go on every target, so there is no stand-in and no library.

The uses are random identifiers and secrets, SHA-256 content digests and derived names, one HMAC-SHA-256 cookie signature, constant-time comparison and a few algorithms fixed by outside formats; each maps to the Go standard library (crypto/rand, crypto/sha256, crypto/hmac, crypto/subtle), under one algorithm policy that an import check enforces. Upstream uses no cipher, key derivation or public-key signature, and neither does the Go design.

Every import is the promise form: cancellable sleeps become a context-aware sleep helper or the cordis timer service, deadlines become context deadlines with a typed cause, and the yields to the single JavaScript thread have no counterpart because goroutines are pre-empted. Tests drive all of it in virtual time with testing/synctest.

Three production files use the monotonic clock only to decide when to yield the single thread, which Go does not need; benchmarks and scripts use it to measure elapsed time, which time.Now with time.Since and testing.B provide. Event-loop delay measurement has no counterpart because there is no event loop.

title: SHA-1 is used as a content identity for captured workspace files and instruction files

reason: The Go algorithm policy makes SHA-256 the only hash for content identity and an import check forbids crypto/sha1 outside the packages that speak an outside format that fixes it, so a constructed SHA-1 collision can no longer make two different files share one stored copy.

title: A minute or hour recurrence rule produces no occurrence during the repeated hour of an autumn clock change

reason: Minute and hour rules accept no BY part and are fixed intervals; the Go evaluator advances them in elapsed time from the start instant, so they keep their spacing through a daylight-saving transition, while daily and longer rules stay in wall time.
